title: Private Deployment: Integration & Security Handoff Checklist
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This checklist captures the minimal technical, security, and operational artifacts that must be verified and handed off between Redwood field engineering and customer security/IT before a private deployment (VPC or on-prem) moves from installation to steady-state operations. It is intended to reduce surprises during Day-2 operations and to provide auditable evidence for compliance reviews.

Scope:
- Applies to Private deployments (VPC, dedicated customer account, air-gapped on-prem) where Redwood control plane or agent components are co-located with customer infrastructure.
- Complements site-specific runbooks and the product release notes.

Owner & escalation
- Document owner: Security (Aisha Patel)
- Field installation owner: Field Delivery (Engineering)
- Primary escalation: field_delivery@redwood.example.com -> security-oncall@redwood.example.com

Prerequisites (before handoff)
1) Signed deployment acceptance form (customer + Redwood delivery lead). Scan of signed PDF attached to ticket.
2) Customer provides a named point of contact and security contact with phone and PGP/GPG public key (if requested).
3) Network and inventory data: public IPs/CIDRs, private service CIDRs, NAT gateways, peering details, and firewall change window.

Key services and expected topology
- redwood-controlplane (managed service endpoint) — if used, confirm TLS fingerprint and endpoint DNS names.
- agent-connector (installed in customer network) — confirm version and boot args.
- telemetry-proxy (local aggregation) — confirm sampling rate and egress rules.
- kms-proxy (optional) — confirm integration type: customer KMS, HSM, or Redwood-managed.

Minimum network and firewall checklist (table)
| Purpose | Protocol/Port | Source | Destination | Required? | Notes |
|---------|---------------|--------|-------------|-----------|-------|
| Agent -> Control Plane | TCP 443 | Customer agents | redwood-controlplane.example.com | Yes | Verify TLS cert fingerprint matches provided value |
| Agent -> Telemetry proxy | TCP 9080 | Agent nodes | telemetry-proxy.local | Yes | Allow only local subnet |
| Metrics scrape | TCP 9100 | monitoring | agent nodes | Optional | Allow from monitoring CIDR only |
| KMS traffic (if customer KMS) | TCP 443 | agent nodes | kms.customer.example | Yes | mTLS strongly recommended |

Identity & authentication
- mTLS between agent-connector and redwood-controlplane is required for customer deployments unless explicitly waived.
- Short-lived service certificates are preferred. Validate CA chain and rotation policy (recommendation: rotate certs every 90 days; emergency rotation < 24h).
- Service account mapping: list of service principals and RBAC roles must be provided and approved. Document the least-privilege roles.

Key material and evidence to collect (each item must have a storage location and owner)
- Installation manifest (YAML) including component images and digests.
- Firmware/BIOS evidence for hosts used in on-prem installs (signed firmware versions).
- KMS integration proof: sample token exchange trace (redacted) and successful encrypt/decrypt evidence.
- TLS certificate fingerprints (PEM, SHA256) for all external endpoints.
- Audit logging endpoints and retention: location + retention policy (must meet customer/regulatory requirement).

Operational SLOs & thresholds to confirm
- API latency: 95th percentile <= 120ms for control-plane calls under normal load profile.
- Availability: 99.9% for agent heartbeat within 5m windows.
- Telemetry sampling: default 1 in 1000 requests; customers may request higher sampling during debugging.
- Disk usage alert: warn at 70% on root and model volumes; critical at 85%.

Acceptance testing (signature tests to run during handoff)
1) End-to-end smoke test (operator-run):
   - Deploy a small test model (<= 512 tokens) to local runtime.
   - API health: curl -s -f -m 10 https://{ingress}/healthz || exit 1
   - Send a sample inference request: 
     curl -s -X POST https://{ingress}/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"test-small","prompt":"hello"}' | jq .status
   - Verify response within SLA and check logs for errors.
2) KV/prefix cache integrity check:
   - Validate that cached prefixes return deterministic tokens for the stored prompt set.
3) Failover validation (optional for multi-zone):
   - Simulate loss of a zone and confirm traffic reroute within 60s and request success rate > 95% during failover window.

Upgrade and rollback guardrails (operational requirements)
- Upgrade window must be scheduled with at least 72 hours notice to customer security and ops.
- Canary plan: upgrade 5% of nodes (or a single non-critical tenant) and monitor these signals for 30 minutes: error rate, latency, model output divergence (basic prompt tests).
- Automated rollback triggers (examples): sustained error rate > 3% for 10 minutes, request latency 3x baseline 95p for 15 minutes, or failing core health checks for 2 consecutive probes.
- Rollback steps (high level):
  1. Pause automated autoscaling and routing.
  2. Initiate backout to previous image/digest.
  3. Rehydrate KV caches where feasible from snapshot or warm path.
  4. Notify customer and begin post-rollback acceptance tests.

Data classification & telemetry policy
- Telemetry categories: metrics (low), traces (medium), logs (medium), request payloads (high).
- Sensitive request payloads must never be forwarded to Redwood-managed telemetry endpoints unless explicit consent is recorded. For customers requiring this, record the consent and the retention window here.
- Retention minimums: logs 90 days (configurable), metrics 365 days (rollup after 90 days).

Post-handoff responsibilities
- Customer security: confirm receipt of all artifacts and sign off on the acceptance tests.
- Redwood field delivery: attach final installation manifest and pointer to images in artifact repo.
- Redwood support: monitor the deployment for 72 hours after handoff (elevated monitoring) and provide a tailored escalation tree.

Templates & artifacts to attach to ticket (required)
- Signed acceptance form (PDF).
- Installation manifest (manifest.yaml).
- TLS and KMS fingerprints (fingerprints.txt).
- Smoke test log output (smoke-test.log).
- Firmware evidence (firmware-evidence.pdf) where applicable.

Common failure modes & mitigation guidance
- Agent fails to authenticate: verify mTLS cert chain, system clock skew (< 60s), and agent configuration file for correct control-plane DNS.
- High tail latency during initial warm-up: confirm KV cache priming and model quantization path; consider temporary routing to a lower-latency variant.
- Telemetry overload: reduce sampling to 1 in 10k and request a targeted snapshot for debugging.

Checklist sign-off (required fields)
- [ ] Customer security sign-off: name, title, date
- [ ] Field delivery sign-off: name, title, date
- [ ] Support assigned: name, roster, 72h monitoring window start/end
- [ ] Artifact attachments: list of files and storage URIs

Appendix A — Example firewall YAML (customer change request snippet)
---
- rule: allow-agent-egress
  src: 10.10.0.0/24
  dst: redwood-controlplane.example.com:443
  proto: tcp
  desc: "Allow outbound to Redwood control plane"
---

Appendix B — Useful quick commands
- Verify TLS fingerprint (SHA256):
  openssl s_client -connect redwood-controlplane.example.com:443 -servername redwood-controlplane.example.com | openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256
- Simple health check:
  curl -s -f -m 10 https://{ingress}/healthz && echo OK || echo FAIL

Related references

- For rollback and upgrade playbooks: see orchestrated-rollforward-and-customer-safeguards.
